chunks: 4763 - Al-Qasim ibn al-Rabiʿ al-Saḥḥāf narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān that Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to him, among what he wrote in reply to his questions:

“The reason for divorce being three times is because of the respite in it between the first and the third, for a desire that may arise, or the subsiding of anger if it was present. And let that be a warning and discipline for women, and a deterrent for them from disobeying their husbands. Thus the woman deserves separation and estrangement for entering into what is not proper through abandoning obedience to her husband.

And the reason for the woman becoming forbidden after nine divorces, such that she is not lawful for him, is as a punishment so that he may not take divorce lightly nor treat the woman as weak. And so that he may be observant in his affairs, vigilant, and reflective, and so that there may be despair for both of them of reunion after nine divorces.”

key_terms.رَغْبَةٍ: renewed inclination or desire for reconciliation
key_terms.غَضَبٍ: anger that may subside before matters become final
key_terms.ٱلطَّلَاقِ: divorce; the legal dissolution of marriage
key_terms.ٱلْمُهْلَةِ: a period of respite or delay allowing reconsideration

ai.seo_question: Why does Islamic law allow divorce in stages and forbid remarriage after nine divorces?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal wisdom behind the staged structure of divorce and the severe consequence attached to repeated divorces. It presents divorce law as a means of reflection, restraint, and deterrence, while also preventing the man from trivializing divorce or wronging the woman.
